body: For petitioner: Mr. Masood Adnan, advocate.
For the State: Mr. Zahid-ul-Haq, Addl: A.G.

,r***** SABIT ULI-/IH J.- 1. The petitioner, Rustam Khan, seeks post-arrest bail under Section 497, Cr.P.C. in case FIR No. 410 dated 2E.O8.2}26,registered under Sections 302,324 and 34, P.P.C. at Police Station Lakki City, District Lakki Marwat. He applied for bail, first before the leamed Additional Sessions Iudge-III, Lakki Marwat, who refused it vide or der dated 22.09.2026.

2. According to the FIR" the complainant, Khurshid Khan, came to the hospital emergency room with the injured minors, Shabnum and Farooq, and reported the occurrence as follows. At about 06:30 a.m. he leamt that the minors had been physically assaulted by their stepbrothers, and he went to the spot to shift them to hospital. An altercation followed. The accused, including the petitioner and coaccused Nazir, then arrived armed with Kalashnikovs and opened fire on the complainant pafiy. The complainant and others received firearm injuries, and the complainant later succumbed to his injuries. The motive was stated to be a dispute over the ancestral house.

3. Leamed counsel for the petitioner mainly relied on three gronnds: the cross-version recorded ,tide Naqal Mad No- I 1 dated 28.08.2026, frie Machalkas produced at the bar, and parity with coaccused Muhammad Aslam Khan. Leamed counsel for the State and the complainant opposed the petition. Arguments have been heard and the record perused.

4. The petitioner is specifically nominated in the FIR' He is attributed effective firing with a Kalashnikov, which is a specific overt act and not mere presence at the spot. That attribution has to be read with the prosecution account, the injuries sustained by the complainant party and the medical evidence on record' At the bail stage the Court is not to determine which weapon caused which injury, to fix individual liability, to find the ultimate motive, or to appraisetheevidenceindepth.Thesemattersfallwithintheexclusive domain of the leamed Trial Court' The only question is whether the material tentatively available fumishes reasonable grounds connecting the petitioner with the offence. A previous family dispute over ancestral property cuts both ways. By itself it neither establishes innocence nor makes the prosecution version doubtful' 5. A counter-version is undoubtedly a relevant circumstance' However, its mere registration does not make the guilt of an accused doubtful or bring his case within the ambit of further inquiry' Each case turns on its own facts. ln Nkar Muhammad Wasan and anolher v. The State (1992 SCMR 501), the Honourable Supreme Court held thatthemereexistenceofcross-FlRsorcross-casesisnogroundfor bail where a specific role is assigned to the accused. The Court relied there on Iqbal Hussain v. Abdul Sattar and another (PLD 1990 SC 758l, which holds that the plea of further inquiry, which can be raised in almost every such case, does not by itself entitle an accused to bail; what matters is a tentative opinion on the merits.

6. The same view was taken in Yar Muhammad Khan v. The State and another (2024 SCMR 1738), where it was held that recording a counter-version in the Roznamcha is no basis for postarrest bail where incriminating material exists. That case also had a positive firearm expert report, which is not shown here, so it is relied on only for the legal principle. It was reiterated in Shehryar Khan v' The State and another (2020 SCMR 1436) that a cross-version whose truth is yet to be settled does not, by itself, bring the case within further probe where a specific role is attributed' Questions arising from a cross-version, and a plea of self-defence, are best left to the Trial Court. The attribution of the fatal shot and the abscondence of the accused in that case are distinguishing features, but the principle applies tully.

7. The Machalkas in counter-version recorded vide Naqal Mad No. 1l dated 28.08.2026 show that Muhammad Sohail son of Amir Khan, Alamgir son of Gul Muhammad and Muhammad Tahir Khan son of Amir Khan were released by the SHO on personal bonds' They have been considered only for the facts recorded in them' Release by the police is neither a judicial finding of innocence nor a decision on themeritsofeitherversion.Withoutmore,itdoesnotdisplacethe specific charge of effective firing against the petitioner' Its evidentiary value, if any, is for the Trial Court to assess' 8, The plea of parity is also misconceived. Co-accused Muhammad Aslam Khan was granted bail by this Court in B.A. No. 445-B/2026, decided on 15.10.2026, because no effective firing was atfibuted to him and he himself was injured, so that his role called for further inquiry. Effective lring was attributed instead to the petitioner and co-accused Nazir. Parity depends on similar roles and circumstances, not merely on being named in the same FIR. Since the petitioner's role is specific and distinct, the concession given to Muhammad Aslam Khan cannot be extended to him.

9. Section 497(2), CI.P.C. applies only where, on a tentative assessment, reasonable grounds to believe the accused committed ttre offence are lacking and there are sufficient grounds for further inquiry into his guilt. Here, the specific attribution of effective firing, read with the prosecution account and the material on record, prima facie connects the petitioner with the offence. That offence falls within the prohibitory clause of Section 497(1), Cr.P.C. The cross-version, the Machalkas and the bail granted to the co-accused, whether taken separately or together, do not weaken that material enough to make out a case of further inquiry.

10. For the foregoing reasons, this petition, being devoid of merit, is dismissed. The observations above are tentative, made only for deciding this bail petition, and shall not prejudice either party at trial. Announced.
